chunks.heading: Central Library
chunks.text:
Central Library
The Kathmandu University Central Library (KUCL) is centrally located in the university central premises and can be reached within three to five minutes from all departments and hostels. The library is housed in a three-story building with a space of about 2290 square meter. The KUCL has majority of books and journals specially related with School of Science and School of Engineering. It monitors services of all libraries of the university.
Schools located in Kathmandu valley and Dhulikhel, have their own libraries to cater the information needs of the students and faculties.

chunks.heading: Objectives
chunks.text:
Objectives
To provide information for the fulfillment of the objectives of the university.
To provide information for teaching, research and management of the university.
To provide learning materials both in conventional and e-resources for study and research.
To adopt ICTs in housekeeping operations of the library.
To manage important documents in Archive mode
To be a full-fledged modern library (e-Library, Digital Library) and connect to all schools, extended & affiliated colleges.
Resource sharing between KU Central library systems to all schools, extended & affiliated colleges

chunks.heading: Collection of Information
chunks.text:
Collection of Information
The library's holdings include over 60,000 volumes of books, 2,500 CD-ROMs, 200 videocassettes, 125 journal titles and newsletters, 20 newspapers and magazines, and 75 audio cassettes, spanning Sciences, Engineering, Management, Teacher Education, Medical Sciences, Arts, and Law.

chunks.heading: Infrastructure provided by library:
chunks.text:

Periodical section, technical processing section, Reference section, Stack-cum-reading room, Circulation section, Offices for librarian and assistant librarian, Store are all well designed. They are all equipped with necessary library furniture and equipment’s designed by the experts.

Spaces:
Reading space,
Book Stack Rooms,
Faculty–Student discussion room,
Arrangement of adequate space for Reference section,
Meeting Hall,
Smart computer Lab,
Archive space,\

chunks.heading: Library Rules and Regulations: > Opening and Closing Hours:
chunks.text:
Library Rules and Regulations: > Opening and Closing Hours:
Library Opening Hours: 7:00AM - 8:00P.M. in weekdays and 12:00 P.M. - 6:00 P.M. on Saturdays and Sundays. The opening hour is subject to change as per needs and circumstances.
Books Circulation Hours: 9:00A.M. - 4:00 P.M. The circulation hour may be adjusted as per need and circumstances.

chunks.heading: Library Rules and Regulations: > Borrowing Rules and Overdue Fines
chunks.text:
Library Rules and Regulations: > Borrowing Rules and Overdue Fines
Books are borrowable for 30 days, and can be renewed once for the same period.
The member is expected to return borrowed books on or before the due date stamped on the date label in the book. An overdue charge will be levied for the late return of the book as follows: No overdue charge for first three days, and for rest of the days Rs. 3/- per vol. per day.
If the due date lies during holidays or vacation period, the book should be returned to the library on the opening day. Failure to return on the opening day is subject to overdue fines of the holidays/vacation period too.

chunks.heading: Library Rules and Regulations: > Card reneual
chunks.text:
Library Rules and Regulations: > Card reneual
In case of loss or damage of the Identity Card, a duplicate card can be made with a fee of Rs. 150.00.
Identity Card should be returned to the library while obtaining library clearance.

chunks.heading: Library Rules and Regulations: > Library Conduct Rules
chunks.text:
Library Rules and Regulations: > Library Conduct Rules
Bags, briefcases, and personal belongings must be left outside the library, and food, drinks, and smoking are not permitted inside. The library maintains a strict quiet policy — conversations, phone calls, and noisy greetings are not allowed. Because the library serves both current and future members, materials are expected to be handled with care.

chunks.heading: Library Rules and Regulations: > Misconduct Penalties
chunks.text:
Library Rules and Regulations: > Misconduct Penalties
Damaging or attempting to steal library materials carries escalating penalties: a first offense results in a fine of either 1,000 rupees or three times the item's value (whichever is higher), a report to the Director of Student Affairs and the notice board, and notification to the student's guardian. A second offense adds suspension of library membership for the remainder of the semester or year and penalties of first offense. A third offense can lead to expulsion proceeding along with penalties of second offense.

chunks.heading: Services Offered:
chunks.text:
Services Offered:
The library provides circulation, inter-library loan, reference and referral services, reprographic (photocopying) services, user education, current awareness services, paper clippings, OPAC catalog search, and internet and email access.

chunks.heading: Internet:
chunks.text:
Internet:
Wi-Fi hotspot available at Library Building inside for all to help them in their study, research and project work.
